text:
Ivy: Noticed a gap in keystore decrypt logs between 03:03-03:15 UTC for onprem-west. No customer-facing errors, but audit objects missing. Tagging SRE-oncall.
Marcus: Which nodes? Any recent changes?
Ivy: ~5 nodes in onprem-west-pool. We pushed both a CMK policy tweak and a netpol tighten during the window.
Lina: Logs from audit-writer show: 
```
2026-03-24T03:05:12Z audit-writer: kms proxy dial failed: connection refused
2026-03-24T03:05:15Z audit-writer: GenerateDataKey failed: AccessDenied
2026-03-24T03:05:16Z audit-writer: buffering to /var/local/audit-buf
```
SRE-oncall: Did the deploy bot run? DevOps-bot?
DevOps-bot: deploy 'onprem-keystore-policy-2026-03-24' by Lina at 03:02 UTC; netpol 'deny-external-egress' merged at 03:01 UTC.
Marcus: Hypothesis: the new netpol blocked pods in the secondary CIDR from reaching kms-proxy; simultaneously CMK policy tightened, so when proxy calls did reach KMS they were denied. Two-layer failure.
Lina: Confirmed: curl to https://kms-proxy:8443/health from affected pod times out; from unaffected pod it returns 200.
Ivy: Mitigation: 1) temporarily revert netpol to allow pod CIDR range 192.168.0.0/20 to proxy, 2) restart audit-writer pods, 3) reupload buffered files.
Marcus: I'll do netpol revert and coordinate reingest. SRE-oncall: snapshot nodes for later forensic.
SRE-oncall: Snapshots created for nodes n-west-01..05 at 03:20 UTC.
Lina: After revert and restart, reingest succeeded for 4/5 nodes; one node had disk rotation so we lost a small batch.
Ivy: Postmortem actions: add CI guard to prevent concurrent network policy + CMK policy changes in same window; add an e2e test that validates GenerateDataKey after any keystore policy change.
Marcus: Also add an alert that flags GenerateDataKey AccessDenied spikes in local audit logs.
DevOps-bot: incident ticket PRIV-KESTORE-GAP-1755556789 created (sev:P2).
Ivy: Thanks team. Closing thread here and linking ticket to postmortem.
